newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil says only to discuss coffee status at ACPC.
newsitem.headline: Brazil says only to discuss coffee status at ACPC.

text.p: The Brazil government will not decide on any position ahead of a coffee producer meeting on March 20 to discuss current high prices and the supply situation, a top government commodities official said.
"We will only discuss the situation there (in London)," said Mauricio Assis, head of the primary commodities department at the Industry and Commerce Ministry.

The technical committee of the Association of Coffee Producing Countries (ACPC) will meet in London to review the market situation and prepare recommendations for the full ACPC council, expected to be held in May.

Indonesia's representative to the ACPC Paian Nainggolan has said the meeting is expected to review a decision taken in Rio de Janeiro in January to cut a further 1.3 million 60-kg bags of coffee from exports in the first six months of this year.
But the Ivory Coast's Commodities Minister Guy-Alain Gauze has subsequently said additional cuts will still be implemented.

Arabica coffee is only to account for 300,000 bags of this total. But given the recent meteoric rise in arabica prices, Brazilian traders have for some time been saying that it is no longer appropriate to rein back exports further.
Assis did not wish to comment on Brazil's position with regard to a possible review of the 1.3 million bag reduction.
He also said that there were no plans for the time being to meet with private sector representatives prior to March 20.

Private sectors officials are next scheduled to meet on March 18 to discusss problems affecting the domestic roasting and soluble coffee industry. -- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
